I have 3.8 mu, not much land. I have been farming it for 6 years now, and I learned everything from my mother-in-law and from watching the neighbors. Last year I put 2.5 mu in chili and 1.3 mu in summer maize, and I will do the exact same thing this year. Chili brings in more cash than grain, but it devours labor and fertilizer. My husband works in a factory in town and my older child is away working, so it is mostly just me and my mother-in-law handling the field. I cannot manage any more chili than the 2.5 mu I already have.

For the chili, I will go to the seed dealer in town and buy the hybrid red thin-skinned seeds — the same ones my neighbor Aunt Zhao planted last year. Her chilies fetched a good price at the market. I will rotary till the soil and lay plastic mulch to keep the heat in, just like everyone else on this block. For the base fertilizer I will spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. When the plants flower I will top-dress with urea twice, about 20 kg each time per mu. The dealer told me potassium helps the fruit set, so I will add 15 kg of potassium chloride per mu too. That comes to about 28 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 18 kg of potassium per mu. I know fertilizer prices went up again this year and I wanted to save some cash for hired picking help in autumn, but two years ago I cut back on fertilizer and the chili was small and worthless. I would rather spend the money now than risk a bad harvest. I will irrigate from my well about 8 times through the hot months, and I will spray pesticide 10 times because the aphids and whiteflies always come — if you skip even one spray they ruin the whole crop. If the weather is normal I should harvest about 2200 kg per mu, same as last year.

For the maize, it is much easier. I will plant hybrid summer maize on the remaining 1.3 mu. At sowing I will put down compound fertilizer, about 40 kg per mu, and at jointing I will top-dress with 25 kg of urea per mu. That is about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Maize does not need much babying. I will irrigate 3 times and spray pesticide 3 times. Last year that gave me 550 kg per mu. I thought about trying a new variety the dealer was pushing, but why take the risk? I will stick with what I know.
